# When a Record Changes (2024 statement)

This page is the earlier statement of the rule. It is kept deliberately: a record that
deletes its own past breaks every citation already pointing at it, and a broken citation
is indistinguishable from a fabricated one.

## What this version said

A document was treated as current until somebody noticed it was not. Currency lived in the
reviewer's head and in the commit history, so a reader arriving from a search engine had
no way to tell a checked-and-current page from a checked-and-overtaken one.

## Why it was replaced

Because the reader is the one who needs to know, and the reader never sees the commit
history. The successor moves that fact onto the page and into the frontmatter, where both
surfaces can read it.

The line that says so is in this document's own frontmatter:

```yaml
superseded_by: when-a-record-changes.md
```

Which is what puts the notice at the top of this page, above everything else on it.
